title: Ramp to the Roof
brief: Sacks go up to roof storage, 1.2 m up: 6 carriers, 2 trolleys, a wheelchair user and an elderly visitor. Everyone must get up. Budget ₹24,000.

mistri.brief: Sacks and wheelchairs both need to get up. Survey the space before you build.

hints.NO_ACCESSIBLE_ROUTE: Stairs do not work for everyone.
hints.RAMP_TOO_STEEP: How steep a slope can a wheelchair manage? Measure first.
hints.TROLLEY_ROLLBACK: A heavy trolley needs a gentle slope.
hints.TIGHT_TURN: A turn needs a full landing, not a corner.
hints.NO_HANDRAIL: What will older visitors hold on to as they climb?
hints.NO_PATH: The route must connect the ground to the roof.
hints.TIME_LIMIT: Watch who moves slowest, and ask why.
hints.default: Measure first: how long must the ramp be, and how much space is there?

insight.title: Accessible design needs space, so plan it first.
insight.principle: A ramp gentle enough for a wheelchair is long. Fold it into a switchback with landings, and give it its space before anything else is built.
insight.example: Well-planned stations and hospitals draw their ramps first. Ramps squeezed in later end up too steep or too tight to turn.
insight.number: 1.2 m up at 1:12 takes 14.4 m of ramp, with a flat landing at least every 9 m.
insight.quote: Plan the ramp first, not last.
